items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: somebody says, hey, you play 'Grandpa's Spells', I just heard it by Liberace.

ctx.x: And for what it started out to do, it was tight and crisp, and I wouldn't call it traditional jazz and the purists probably didn't like it. But there was a lot of people that liked it and bought it. And the record don't come out. We wait month after month after month and it's still ain't out.

Now I go up to Minneapolis to play a date, and somebody says, hey, you play 'Grandpa's Spells', I just heard it by Liberace. And then I get back to Chicago and the band leader, the A&R man, has put out a record. What they did was, they heard me do 'Grandpa's Spells', and they loved the material. So somebody got Liberace to do it. Then their A&R man did it, then after they milked it, then they put out my record.
